chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the As-Sa'ibah, so he said: 'Look at what is in the Quran; whatever has in it

That, O 'Ammar, is the Sa'ibah which has no guardianship for anyone upon it except Allah. And whatever its guardianship is for Allah, it is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and whatever is for his Messenger, then indeed its guardianship is for the Imam, and its liability is upon the Imam, and its inheritance is for him.

key_terms.اَلسَّائِبَة: A slave freed by their master with no obligation to serve them in return, often with specific inheritance rules.
key_terms.اَلْإِمَام: The Imam, who holds the guardianship and inheritance rights of the Sa'ibah in this context.
key_terms.تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَة: The freeing of a slave (neck), a key concept in Islamic jurisprudence regarding manumission.
key_terms.وَلَاء: Guardianship or kinship rights, particularly the right to inherit and manage the estate of the freed person.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Sa'ibah and who inherits their estate according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of the *Sa'ibah* by linking the Quranic phrase 'freeing of a neck' (4:92) to a unique chain of guardianship (*wilayah*) that culminates in the Imam. This hadith establishes the theological principle that just as the Prophet’s *wilayah* is derived from Allah’s, the Imam’s authority over the estate and liabilities of such freed slaves is an extension of divine sovereignty, reinforcing the concept of *Al-Wilayah al-Takwiniyyah* in Shia jurisprudence.
